Continuous color scale using koloRo palettes

Source: R/ggplot2-scales.R
scale_color_koloro_c.Rd

Apply a koloRo palette as a continuous color gradient in ggplot2. Useful for representing continuous numeric data.

Usage

scale_color_koloro_c(palette = "viridis", direction = 1, ...)

scale_colour_koloro_c(palette = "viridis", direction = 1, ...)

Arguments

palette

Character string specifying the palette name. Default is "viridis".

direction

Integer. If 1 (default), colors are used as-is. If -1, the order of colors is reversed.

...

Additional arguments passed to ggplot2::scale_color_gradientn().

Value

A ggplot2 scale object.

References

Wickham, H. (2016). ggplot2: Elegant graphics for data analysis (2nd ed.). Springer-Verlag. doi:10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)

# Basic usage with viridis
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_koloro_c()

# Use plasma palette
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_koloro_c("plasma")

# Use Alhambra sunset palette
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_koloro_c("alhambra_sunset")
} # }
